subject: Re: Micro-call minimums and sparsity reconciliation
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@prismretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Prism Retail Procurement <procurement@prismretail.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Micro-call billing spike — can you help reconcile?

Hi Dylan,

Hope you're well. We pulled our December invoice and saw a noticeable bump tied to a very large number of very short generation calls (many under ~12 tokens). Team is confused how micro-call minimums and token rounding applied — the numbers don't line up with our expectations from the SOW.

Attached is a filtered usage extract (usage-extract-202612.csv) showing call-level rows and token counts. Key questions:
- Are micro-call minimums applied per request or aggregated across the same session?
- How does sub-token rounding work for short streaming calls — do you round each call up to the minimum?
- Would a high-volume of sub-24-token calls be charged as a block or individually?

We want to understand whether this is a metering artifact (rounding/quantum) or a packaging mismatch. Can someone on your side walk us through a reconciliation with simple worked examples? If there are quick mitigations (e.g., prefix caching or batching recommendations) please call those out.

Thanks — Anita

Subject: Re: Micro-call billing spike — can you help reconcile?

Hi Anita — thanks for the extract, that helps. Looping in Marissa and Irene from Billing/Finance so we can give a concrete answer with examples. Initial comments below, we’ll follow up with a reconciliation table early tomorrow.

Short answers up front:
- Micro-call minimums are applied per request by default (each call is evaluated against the floor).
- Sub-token rounding depends on the metering quantum for the model: tokens are bucketed into the defined quantum, and we round up to that quantum per billed unit.
- For streaming calls, the same rounding rules apply per billed unit; we do not collapse many tiny calls into a single billed quantum unless they are part of the same pinned session and KV cache reuse is detected.

Quick ask for you so Irene can run examples:
1) Can you confirm if the calls in the CSV are independent HTTP requests (yes/no)?
2) Any client-side retry patterns within 1–2s that might look like many calls but are duplicates?

I attached a short explainer (redwood-billing-explainer.pdf) with the current floor rules and a sample invoice mapping. We can propose a temporary concession if the pattern looks like an onboard artifact.

Next steps: Irene will produce worked examples (sample line-item walk-through) and I’ll coordinate a formal concession proposal for procurement if warranted.

Best,
Dylan

Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Micro-call billing spike — can you help reconcile? (worked examples)

Dylan — forwarding my worked examples and recommendation. Quoting your note for context:

> - Micro-call minimums are applied per request by default (each call is evaluated against the floor).

Worked examples (simplified):
- Metering quantum: 16 tokens (example model), micro-call floor: 1 quantum per call.
- If a request consumes 5 tokens -> billed as 16 tokens (1 quantum).
- If user issues 10 separate 5-token calls -> billed as 10 * 16 = 160 tokens.
- If same 10 calls are routed inside a pinned session and we detect KV cache reuse + you pin model session, we may aggregate where prefix caching reduces effective compute; however the billed quantum is still applied per individually metered request unless explicit session aggregation is used.

Sub-token rounding note: our meter works in fixed quanta. There is no fractional carry between HTTP requests. That means high-frequency microcalls appear highly inefficient on token bills.

Recommendation & proposed concession for Prism Retail (to smooth onboarding friction):
- Temporary concession: For the first 90 days after the January invoice, apply a microcall credit equal to the difference between per-request quantum billing and an aggregated-billing baseline for calls <24 tokens.
  - Implementation: Finance will calculate the "microcall delta" and apply as a credit line on next invoice.
- If Prism wants a permanent fix, we can:
  1) Recommend SDK batching/prefix batching patterns (engineering change), OR
  2) Move Prism onto a small dedicated allocation where we can enable session aggregation and a lower quantum for high-volume microcalls (operational change + commitment).

I attached a mock invoice CSV (prism_pricing_sample_invoice_Q4.csv) with a column-by-column mapping that ties the raw CSV rows to invoice lines (shows the delta and the proposed credit calculation).

If approved, Ben/Marissa: please confirm the credit cap (I suggest cap at $15k overall for the 90-day pilot) and whether procurement needs a formal credit memo.

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-01-12T15:33:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Micro-call billing spike — reconciliation and temporary credit proposal

Hi Anita — thanks again for the CSV and for flagging this. Summary and proposal below so procurement has a single clear ask.

Findings (short):
- December’s spike is almost entirely explained by a very large number of independent microcalls (median token usage ~6).
- Our metering quantum (16-token blocks for the model used) means each of those microcalls is rounded up to the 16-token quantum.
- No evidence in the CSV of automated de-dupe/retry patterns; calls look like separate client requests.

Proposal (operational + commercial):
1) Commercial concession (temporary): Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to the calculated microcall delta for calls <24 tokens for Dec–Feb (90 days). Credit cap: $15,000.
2) Operational remediation: we recommend the engineering team adopt SDK batching (we’ll share code snippets) or switch the highest-volume paths to a pinned session flow to take advantage of KV cache reuse.
3) Long-term option: move Prism to a dedicated pool where we can reduce the quantum and/or enable per-session aggregation (requires 6–12 month commitment).

Action items:
- Procurement: please confirm acceptance of the $15k cap and whether a formal credit memo (DocuSign) is required.
- Anita / Integrations: If you want the code snippets for batching, reply and I’ll route a short engineering note.
- Marissa / Irene / Ben: please confirm the credit calculation and next invoice application.

If that works, I’ll draft a short concession letter and route to procurement.

Thanks,
Dylan
